notes: Deploy the accepted src/SelloutMachine.sol on Ethereum mainnet. Its sole nonpayable constructor argument is the owner address the brief states, 0xCcf0a1307E5e5Ad04E85d94d7f9D400390F0118a, written as a static address rather than $owner because the owner is immutable with no transfer path and the brief names it explicitly; this removes any dependency on how $owner resolves. That wallet holds exclusive immutable configuration authority. There are no constructor dependencies, deployment ETH, initialization calls, tokens, pools, proxies or ownership transfers. The tracked collection starts unset and Craft #10000's 10,000-byte payload is all white. The owner selects or changes a compatible ERC-721 through setTrackedCollection(address) on Etherscan without redeployment or reattachment. Supply is read dynamically, capped at 10,000; failed reads display white and burns may reverse progress. Pixel bytes are row-major, 0x00 black then 0xff white. Do not automatically attach the Machine or modify The Vessel. After deployment, the Craft holder or Vessel-appointed delegate may call setMachineHolder(10000, deployedMachine) on Vessel 0xECb92Cc7112b80A2234936315BbB493fb48d1463 after checking Craft state. See docs/deployment.md for owner operations, docs/security-review.md for the accepted review, and docs/verification.md and docs/gas.md for test evidence and benchmarks; where those documents say the constructor argument is supplied as $owner, this manifest's static address supersedes them. Vessel's existing full SVG renderer has substantial gas cost; successful payload integration does not establish public RPC rendering availability. Mainnet deployment, explorer verification and publication receipts remain launch-stage deliverables.
